live_version_coupling.mechanism: Inside withLockedFinancialProxy's db.transaction: the live row is updated, then updateCurrentFinancialProxyVersion writes toVersionReviewStatus(newStatus) to the current version, then assertLiveVersionStatusCoupling(updated.reviewStatus, version.reviewStatus) runs. All three are in the SAME transaction, so a coupling violation throws and rolls back.
live_version_coupling.mapping_is_the_frozen_one: The live token crosses into the version write ONLY through toVersionReviewStatus. For this route's transition that is 'pending_review' -> 'under_review', exactly the frozen live_to_version_review_status_mapping.

organization_scoping.at_733d3b3f: The primitive's own checks: `if (proxy.organizationId && proxy.organizationId !== ctx.organization.id) throw 'Forbidden'` and `if (!proxy.organizationId) throw 'Forbidden'` (system/global proxies are admin-only). Correct on the security axis but wrong on this route's frozen response contract — see D2.

failure_behavior.mapping: The route maps three named primitive errors to its frozen contract: 'Proxy not found' -> 404, 'Unexpected current status' -> 400 already_submitted, 'Forbidden' -> 403. Any other error is rethrown, reaching the outer handler which returns the identity layer's own status for AuthContextError and 500 otherwise. No error is swallowed.
failure_behavior.requireFromStatus_is_in_transaction: CONFIRMED and load-bearing. The 'must currently be suggested' precondition is evaluated against the LOCKED row inside the transition closure, not as a separate pre-read. The pre-R-B2-10 code did a separate SELECT then UPDATE, whose race window (an admin approval landing between them would silently regress an approved proxy to pending_review) is closed by construction.

locking_select_semantics.change: withLockedFinancialProxy's row-lock SELECT predicate becomes `and(eq(id, proxyId), eq(organizationId, options.organizationId))` when options.organizationId is supplied, instead of `eq(id, proxyId)`. cross_tenant_404_behavior.before_R4: 403 Forbidden — which confirms to the caller that the id exists and belongs to another tenant.
cross_tenant_404_behavior.after_R4: 404 Proxy not found — indistinguishable from an id that does not exist.
cross_tenant_404_behavior.adversarial_case_covered: An actor holding ACTIVE membership in BOTH the requesting and the owning organization still receives 404 while acting under the requesting organization's context, because the predicate keys on ctx.organization.id (the SELECTED, re-derived organisation) alone and never on 'any organisation this user belongs to'. Verified against the predicate itself, not against the commit message.

IDOR_resistance_independently_reproduced.ER_concern: Whether organizationId reaching the lock predicate could be influenced by request input, which would turn the new scoping into an IDOR vector rather than a defence.
provenance_trace_performed_by_this_sessi: app/api/proxies/[id]/suggest/route.ts:16 — `const ctx = await getCurrentOrganizationContext()`. Null -> 401. `ctx` is the ONLY tenancy input to the primitive; `params.id` is the resource id and never a tenancy value.

lib/auth/session.ts:213 — getCurrentOrganizationContext returns { user, membership, organization } built solely from loadRequestPrincipal(); it accepts no arguments at all, so no request value can reach it.
lib/auth/database-context.ts:441 -> resolveRequestPrincipal — identity comes from getVerifiedAuthIdentityResult(); no identity -> null principal.

lib/auth/database-context.ts:391-414 — readPrincipalUnderOpenContext calls getSelectedOrganizationId(), whose in-repository comment states the S3 REQUEST_PRINCIPAL_CONTRACT explicitly: 'The carrier is an ASSERTION ONLY — reaching this line proves nothing by itself; every membership below is re-derived from live database state.' The selected id is then passed to loadActiveMembershipWithinContext(userId, selectedOrganizationId); if no ACTIVE membership exists for that pair the principal resolves to membership null / organization null, and the route returns 401.
IDOR_resistance_independently_reproduced.conclusion: ctx.organization.id is a SERVER-DERIVED value, re-derived per request against organization_members and gated on active membership. An attacker who forges the selection carrier for an organisation they are not an active member of does not obtain that context at all — they get 401, never a scoped lookup into that tenant. An attacker who supplies another tenant's proxy id gets 404 because the predicate excludes the row. Neither reaches a cross-tenant write. NO IDOR.
IDOR_resistance_independently_reproduced.second_independent_layer: The route additionally executes inside withOrganizationDatabaseContext, so PostgreSQL RLS scopes the session independently of the application predicate. The 404 contract does not rest on a single control.

open_findings_non_blocking.location: lib/pipeline/proxies.ts, the ternary at the end of updateFinancialProxyReviewStatusForContext (approximately lines 780-788)
open_findings_non_blocking.measurement: `const result = newStatus === 'approved' ? await withExpectedLockedFinancialProxy(proxyId, expectedApprovalState, authorize, transition) : await withLockedFinancialProxy(proxyId, transition, hideCrossTenantAsNotFound ? {...} : undefined)`. The 'approved' branch never receives options.organizationId, so a caller passing hideCrossTenantAsNotFound=true together with newStatus='approved' would silently get the old 403 leak instead of 404.
